statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-96225 (GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2) is a .NET elevation of privilege issue in the runtime (Microsoft.NETCore.App, System.Private.CoreLib): on Unix, the named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symbolic-link races and unsafe permission changes, so a local attacker can truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions or elevate privileges. Microsoft lists Linux and macOS as the affected platforms and the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/476, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135706, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. Every build ships System.Private.CoreLib.dll and libcoreclr.so at its own .NET version. The seven System.Private.CoreLib.dll copies per build and architecture are in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet10-runtime and, in dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, in the .NET SDK's shared framework, the runtime pack and NativeAOT runtime pack (each as a nupkg, and the NativeAOT pack also installed in the SDK) and the .NET and ASP.NET Core runtime archives; the five libcoreclr.so files are in the same two shared frameworks, the runtime pack and the two runtime archives. No copy from another .NET version is present. That version is 10.0.2 to 10.0.10 in the first nine builds and 10.0.13 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on (for example, System.Private.CoreLib.dll and libcoreclr.so carry version 10.0.1026.32716 in 10.0.10-r0 and 10.0.1326.50504 in 10.0.13-r0 on both architectures). The fix is dotnet/dotnet commit 46e12b57000895ce6d079112888fdc3e68198481 on release/10.0.1xx ("Fixes for Shared Mutex privileges/permissions"), which changes the shared-memory and named-mutex code compiled into libcoreclr.so and the Unix Mutex code in System.Private.CoreLib; it is in the v10.0.113 source tag and not in v10.0.112 (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/46e12b57000895ce6d079112888fdc3e68198481). Every libcoreclr.so and System.Private.CoreLib.dll records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from, and on both architectures that is the v10.0.110 tag in 10.0.10-r0 and the v10.0.113 tag in 10.0.13-r0. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-96225 (GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2) is a .NET elevation of privilege issue in the runtime (Microsoft.NETCore.App, System.Private.CoreLib): on Unix, the named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symbolic-link races and unsafe permission changes, so a local attacker can truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions or elevate privileges. Microsoft lists Linux and macOS as the affected platforms and the .NET 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32, and the .NET 8.0.32 release notes list this CVE (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/476, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135706, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). Between the dotnet/runtime v8.0.31 and v8.0.32 tags, the shared-mutex code in the CoreCLR platform layer (sharedmemory.cpp and mutex.cpp) changes in 'Fixes for Shared Mutex privileges/permissions', which stops changing permissions on globally visible directories and stops following symbolic links when it validates and fixes them (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/3928fdb88d27fbbd7591f558bcf90b12624944a4, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/compare/v8.0.31...v8.0.32). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. Per build and architecture there are four System.Private.CoreLib.dll files, in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet8-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap and in the runtime pack and NativeAOT compiler pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and four libcoreclr.so files, in the same two shared frameworks, the runtime pack and the Crossgen2 pack; the runtime pack directory inside that SDK links to the SDK's shared-framework copies. Every one of these files carries the build's own .NET version, and no copy from another .NET version is present. libcoreclr.so names the dotnet/runtime commit it was built from: v8.0.31 (1219a42122cf) in 8.0.31-r0 and v8.0.32 (b9a49e4a6d3a), which contains the shared-mutex change, in 8.0.32-r0; the earlier builds carry 8.0.23 to 8.0.29 and the later builds 8.0.33 and 8.0.34. The range ends at 8.0.32-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
